raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"From Hôtel de Sully, carry on toward Musée Carnavalet — it's about a six-minute walk.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Three centuries ago, one of the greatest letter writers in French literature sat out in this very garden with pen and paper, utterly delighted by the place.","source_id":"5f99e75f-a5cf-45e3-a9de-cd5757072538","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"That was Madame de Sévigné, born 1626, died 1696, and she spent the last twenty years of her life in this hôtel, writing many of her letters outdoors, in the shadow of her home.","source_id":"5f99e75f-a5cf-45e3-a9de-cd5757072538","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"'It is an admirable affair,' she wrote, 'we shall all stay here and enjoy the fine air.'","source_id":"5f99e75f-a5cf-45e3-a9de-cd5757072538","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"'Since it is impossible to have everything, we shall have to dispense with parquet floors and fashionable little stoves; but at least we have a fine courtyard, a beautiful garden, and nice little blue girls who are most convenient.'","source_id":"5f99e75f-a5cf-45e3-a9de-cd5757072538","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"The 'blue girls' were nuns in blue habits, from a convent on what's now rue Sévigné — then rue Sainte-Catherine — where the Lycée Victor-Hugo stands today.","source_id":"5f99e75f-a5cf-45e3-a9de-cd5757072538","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"This was the Marais of the seventeenth century, when the nearby church of Saint-Paul-Saint-Louis was the stage for some of the greatest preaching and music of the age.","source_id":"0b159876-f314-42d3-a54e-7da4f6388597","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Step into the courtyard of Carnavalet and you're surrounded by one of the most formidable historic buildings in the whole Marais.","source_id":"b9409960-24d9-4b76-96fc-3fe3ed3c1080","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"It went up in 1546 under the spell of the Italian Renaissance, two wings set at right angles, looking out over a strict, symmetrical little French garden.","source_id":"b9409960-24d9-4b76-96fc-3fe3ed3c1080","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"On the main façade opposite the entrance, four stone reliefs — The Seasons — are the work of Jean Goujon, the Renaissance sculptor who lived from 1510 to 1564 and whom Bernini himself admired.","source_id":"b9409960-24d9-4b76-96fc-3fe3ed3c1080","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Goujon also carved the decorations on the southwest side of the Louvre's square courtyard, the Cour Carré, and on the façade of its ground-floor reception room.","source_id":"b9409960-24d9-4b76-96fc-3fe3ed3c1080","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Inside, the museum and the adjoining Hôtel le Peletier de Fargeau lay out the whole history of Paris.","source_id":"d01ea1c1-1449-439d-a902-99bfe41f13a8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Up on the first floor, room 21 recreates Sévigné's own apartments — her writing desk, and portraits of her and her literary friends.","source_id":"d01ea1c1-1449-439d-a902-99bfe41f13a8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"After her death, though, her prim descendants sugarcoated some of her letters before publishing them.","source_id":"d01ea1c1-1449-439d-a902-99bfe41f13a8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"The same thing happened in England, where the prissy daughter of Lady Mary Wortley Montagu 'edited' her mother's brilliant Embassy Letters of 1763 — a correspondence Voltaire rated even higher than Sévigné's.","source_id":"d01ea1c1-1449-439d-a902-99bfe41f13a8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Carnavalet is one example of a whole new kind of home that took over the Marais from the Renaissance on.","source_id":"8f1ed4eb-c9e4-44e6-b602-5f9bbef882a1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Wealthy families bought up the land, walled each plot, and cut an entrance wide enough for a horse and carriage.","source_id":"8f1ed4eb-c9e4-44e6-b602-5f9bbef882a1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Behind it lay a courtyard with room to turn the carriage, then the house, and behind that the garden.","source_id":"8f1ed4eb-c9e4-44e6-b602-5f9bbef882a1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"The whole point was to live tucked between courtyard and garden, sealed off from the filth, noise and bustle of the Paris streets.","source_id":"8f1ed4eb-c9e4-44e6-b602-5f9bbef882a1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"They called them hôtels particuliers — private town houses — and many, like this one, survive as museums.","source_id":"8f1ed4eb-c9e4-44e6-b602-5f9bbef882a1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2}]}
